text: {"headline":"Elevated 99215 billing at every complexity tier, including many low-complexity visits, but documentation is too thin to separate upcoding from a sicker panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The 99215 share runs well above the all-provider rate in nearly every complexity tier (except 5+), and over a third of 99215s fall on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions. Several sampled examples are single routine diagnoses such as I10, E11.9 or E78.5 (e.g., C0024436, C0024665, C0024669), which is the pattern most consistent with upcoding. Against that, the few charts returned all supported the billed level, including high-MDM 99215s on a low-complexity claim (C0024646) and a high-complexity claim (C0024533). That is too small a documented sample to lean either way, and the 3 moderate-plus data-reviewed notes with no lab or test line are weak evidence of possible templated documentation, not proof. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims (starting with C0024436, C0024604, C0024638 and C0024665), check whether MDM and time are genuinely supported, and look for cloned note language across visits."}
